subject: Partner integration revenue splits — tiered escrow & intro-validation flow
messages:
From: Ravi Singh <ravi.singh@bytebridge.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, May 17, 2027 at 09:12 AM PDT
Subject: Partnership revenue-share + lead validation proposal

Hi Marissa / Karthik,

Great to meet you both at the meetup last week. ByteBridge is excited about embedding Redwood inference into our marketplace — strong developer demand and several pilot buyers already. Before we jump into engineering, we wanted to get alignment on commercial mechanics so we can forecast.

High-level ask:
- Revenue-share on new customer subscriptions introduced by ByteBridge (we currently expect most deals to be first-year subscriptions).
- A simple lead-registration / intro-validation window to protect our sourced opportunities.
- An escrow/holdback to account for chargebacks and short-term churn.

Attached is our standard term sheet that shows our preferred splits and sample language (Initial_Term_Sheet.docx). We put a placeholder of 12% referral fee + 6% ongoing reseller margin for joint-sold deals as a starting point, but were flexible.

Can you share what a typical Redwood partner slab looks like, and any constraints (minimums, clawback windows, proof-of-intro requirements)? If it helps, Asha Patel (cc) is our partnerships lead and will coordinate onboarding.

Thanks,
Ravi Singh
Head of Alliances, ByteBridge
ravi.singh@bytebridge.io
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ravi Singh <ravi.singh@bytebridge.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, May 17, 2027 at 11:03 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Partnership revenue-share + lead validation proposal

Thanks Ravi — great to hear. Looping in Ben from Partner Ops & Karthik on commercial mechanics.

Quick reply with a proposed framework (we can convert to an MOU once you sign off):
1) Commission structure (tiered):
   - Referral (bring-intro): 10% of first-year ARR for self-sourced leads verified within the registration window.
   - Reseller margin (where ByteBridge invoices & handles support): 15% margin on net platform revenue for the first year, 8% on renewals.
   - Volume tier: if cumulative ARR introduced by ByteBridge exceeds $1M in a 12-month period, standard referral rises +2% on subsequent deals.
2) Lead registration and intro-validation:
   - 90-day registration window from first substantive touch (email sequence or signed NDA).
   - Registration form + ticket in our partner portal (we require at least two touchpoints and a short qualification note).
3) Escrow / holdback:
   - We propose a 60-day holdback where 50% of the commission is placed in escrow to protect against chargebacks/invalidations. After 60 days the balance is released unless there's a documented claim.
4) Clawback / chargebacks:
   - If a customer cancels/credits within 90 days and Redwood issues a refund, associated partner commission is prorated and recouped.
5) Operational notes:
   - API keys and partner seats can be made available for sandboxing during onboarding.
   - Well need an SOW for any co-delivered engineering work.

I attached a simple commission_slab.xlsx and a draft SOW for your team to review. If ByteBridge is OK with the 60-day hold, we can draft an MOU and aim for a pilot credit and joint announcement within 6 weeks.

Next steps: can Asha confirm preferred legal contact and any internal approval timelines?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Channel Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 (650) 555-0199

---
Attachments: commission_slab.xlsx (attachment), ByteBridge_SOW_v1.pdf (attachment)

Couple of operational/legal questions before we lock these numbers in — tagging Laura for legal and finance read: 

- Definition of converted ARR: are we counting gross contract value or net after discounts/refunds? We should standardize to net-recognized revenue for Redwood invoices.
- Escrow mechanics: do we want Redwood to administer the escrow (book as a deferred liability) or use a third-party escrow vendor? Finance will prefer Redwood-administered ledger if volumes are small.
- Clawback cadence: suggest we mirror billing cadence (quarterly reconciliations) and include a 12-month lookback cap on recoupments for material disputes.
- Proof of intro: examples we accept: signed NDA, signed quote, or HubSpot deal created with first-touch notes. The registration form must include the HubSpot link so we have traceability.

I'll draft a short ops-checklist and a revenue accounting note — attaching for review. If legal wants stricter language, we can add a 30/60/90 day escrow release schedule for specific categories (trial churn vs billing disputes).

Ben Carter
Partner Operations | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Ravi Singh <ravi.singh@bytebridge.io>

Date: Thu, May 20, 2027 at 03:34 PM PDT
Subject: Re: Partnership revenue-share + lead validation proposal

Marissa / Ben / Karthik — thanks, all. We reviewed the slab and ops checklist with our CFO and partnerships team. High level were aligned, a few clarifications so legal can move fast:

1) Escrow admin: ByteBridge prefers Redwood to administer the escrow ledger for speed, but wed like quarterly statements showing holds and releases.
2) Clawback cap: the 12-month lookback is fine, but can you make the cap at 100% of the disputed commission (i.e., no retroactive clawback beyond amounts paid)?
3) API access: for sandbox + service verification, we need partner-level API tokens and a policy doc for rate limits. Can you provision a sandbox token and share the partner usage doc?

If you can confirm the above, our legal will sign the MOU and wed like to start a pilot the week of June 21 (2-person engineering trial + pilot credit).

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

— Ravi
Head of Alliances, ByteBridge
